solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Snakes biting one below backside? Get potent antiseptics

indicators.note: something biting holds a morsel between its jaws, so the snakes word closes around the rest
in a down entry, a part placed below another simply follows it in the light

blocks.note: a common informal word for the buttocks
one as the indefinite article
snakes as a verb: moves stealthily along

explanation.surface: Someone bitten on the bottom by snakes is told to find strong antiseptics.
explanation.walkthrough: Snakes is a verb here, not the reptiles. Cassareep is a thick Guyanese sauce of boiled cassava juice, valued as a preservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassareep, made from cassava juice, has strong antiseptic properties and is used to preserve meat in pepperpot stews.

clue.text: Fervent campaigners judge is to incarcerate I understood

indicators.note: to incarcerate is to lock up inside, so the outer letters hold the rest

blocks.note: J is the standard abbreviation for judge
taken as written
taken as written
as in 'I had it', meaning I grasped it

explanation.surface: Zealous activists say a judge plans to jail someone who claims to have understood.
explanation.walkthrough: J and IS together hold I HAD: J-I HAD-IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Jihadis are militants waging a holy war, so zealous fighters for a cause.

clue.text: Illustrated work's US authors entertaining new read

indicators.note: a host entertaining a guest has them inside, so these letters surround the next

blocks.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer, made plural
hot off the press, i.e. fresh
to read out is to say

explanation.surface: A book of American writers has a fresh read inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: P-HOT-OES, then SAY. The 's after 'work' is 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A photo-essay tells a story mainly through a sequence of photographs, so it is a pictorial piece of journalism.

clue.text: Served up nuts and raisins for US TV show

indicators.note: in a down entry, served up means sent upwards, so the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: gorp is the American name for trail mix of nuts and dried fruit

explanation.surface: American trail mix is served as a snack for television viewers.
explanation.definitionFit: Prog is a British informal clipping of programme, a broadcast show.

clue.text: Arranged the broadcast supported by excellent Greek entertainers

indicators.note: things arranged are put into a new order, so the following word is reordered
in a down entry, being supported means having something underneath, so the next part follows

blocks.note: the three letters reordered
to air a programme is to broadcast it
A1 means first-class, with the 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A programme is put together with top-class Greek performers.
explanation.definitionFit: Hetairai were educated courtesans of ancient Greece who provided company and entertainment for wealthy men.

clue.text: Champion showing how to make pot?

blocks.note: first meaning: excellent, as an adjective
second meaning, cryptic: turn a three-letter word upside down and it reads as pot

explanation.walkthrough: Tip the word TOP over and it reads POT, so TIP TOP is the instruction. The question mark flags this playful second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Champion as an adjective means first-rate, and tip-top is a colloquial synonym for excellent.

clue.text: Start to cook with foremost of olive oils

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters are mixed into a new order
the foremost part of a word is its opening letter alone

blocks.note: taken as written, ready for mixing
the opening letter of olive

explanation.surface: A cookery instruction: begin by cooking with the best olive oils.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottar is a variant of attar, the fragrant essential oil distilled from rose petals.

clue.text: Model stripped to show muscles, European and a remarkable specimen naked

indicators.note: something naked has its covering removed, so the word loses its outer letters

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
informally, a scorcher is something outstanding

explanation.surface: An anatomical figure shows its muscles, like a fine European specimen without clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Scorcher is British slang for anything outstanding, as well as a very hot day. The word 'and' just joins the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: An écorché is an artist's figure of a body drawn or sculpted without skin, displaying the musculature.

clue.text: Monkeys climbing up deer spotted in summer

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing up means the word runs from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: sakis are South American monkeys with bushy tails

explanation.surface: Monkeys scramble up while deer are seen in the summer.
explanation.definitionFit: The sika is an Asian deer whose coat shows white spots in its summer colouring.

clue.text: Plant drifting in sea

indicators.note: drifting things float out of place, so these letters move into a new order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A piece of vegetation is floating in the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Anise is a Mediterranean herb of the carrot family grown for its liquorice-flavoured seeds.

clue.text: Exposed one taking drugs losing head

indicators.note: losing its head means a word drops its opening letter

blocks.note: one as the indefinite article
slang for being high on stimulants

explanation.surface: Someone on drugs was found out after losing their head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking drugs' reads as an action, but it stands for a single slang adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To air something is to expose it to view or to the open air, so aired means exposed.

clue.text: Avid Merrion's first to go bunking off to the local

indicators.note: the first of a name is just its opening letter
a letter that has to go is removed from the word

blocks.note: the opening letter of Merrion
mitching is a dialect word in Wales and Ireland for playing truant

explanation.surface: A keen Merrion leaves school early to go down to the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The local' looks like the pub, but here it means local dialect. Bunking off is British slang for skipping school.
explanation.definitionFit: Itching to do something means being eager or impatient for it, which is what avid conveys.

clue.text: Watercourse often dried up in this hot terrain

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the following words, spanning their letters

blocks.note: found across the end of the first word, the whole second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A stream that often runs dry in such a scorching landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: A shott is a shallow salt lake or marsh in North Africa that dries out in the hot season.

clue.text: Blokes over 30 in Orkney

indicators.note: turned over, so the word is read back to front

blocks.note: oiks is British slang for uncouth men

explanation.surface: Men past thirty living in the Orkney Islands.
explanation.walkthrough: '30' looks like an age, but it points to the answer at 30-across, SHED.
explanation.definitionFit: Skio is an Orkney and Shetland dialect word for a hut or shed.

clue.text: Seven anthems of Chesterfield perhaps, voice to embrace God

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in the arms, so these letters wrap around the next

blocks.note: O is a shortened form of of, as in will-o'-the-wisp
a chesterfield is a type of padded couch
to give voice to a feeling is to vent it
D is an abbreviation of Latin Deus

explanation.surface: A set of seven church anthems from Chesterfield, a voice holding God.
explanation.walkthrough: Chesterfield looks like the Derbyshire town but is a sofa; the insertion straddles the join between two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The O Antiphons, sung in the last seven days of Advent before Christmas, each begin with the exclamation O.

clue.text: Computing expert supposedly hacking terminals in reports from Russian news agency

indicators.note: hacking means chopping off, so letters are cut from the word
terminals are the end points, so only the outer letters are meant

blocks.note: IT is information technology
a smart-ass is a know-all, someone who thinks himself an expert
the very ends of the run reports from

explanation.surface: A computing whizz is said to be hacking into the reports of a Russian news agency.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters to remove come from the clue itself: the outer pair of the phrase 'reports from'.
explanation.definitionFit: ITAR-TASS was the name of the Russian state news agency from 1992 until it reverted to TASS.

clue.text: Force in absent staff overturning company doctor?

indicators.note: something overturning flips over, so the word is read backwards
in places one element inside another

blocks.note: A is the register abbreviation for absent
a staff is a stick or rod
vis is Latin for force, used in English

explanation.surface: A missing employee knocks over the firm's medic with force.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the staff word is turned over; the abbreviation for absent stays at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A company doctor is a consultant brought in to fix an ailing business, a kind of advisor, hence the question mark.

clue.text: What'll halt your masochistic practices, Peter?

blocks.note: first meaning: an agreed word to stop a bondage scene
second meaning: peter is criminal slang for a strongbox, so it is literally a word meaning strongbox

explanation.walkthrough: Peter looks like a man being addressed, but it is a slang term for a strongbox, so it is a word for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Partners in BDSM agree a code word that ends play at once; and peter is a criminal slang term for a strongbox.

clue.text: Stones forming basis to copy hip-hop CD?

blocks.note: to rip a CD is to copy its tracks to a computer
rap is hip-hop music, here the music on the disc

explanation.surface: A rapper's collection of gems is the foundation for pirating a hip-hop album.
explanation.definitionFit: Riprap is loose broken stone laid as a foundation or to protect a bank or breakwater from erosion.

clue.text: Plant carpet in hall

indicators.note: in places one element inside another

blocks.note: aula is a dictionary word for a hall
a rug is a small carpet

explanation.surface: A potted plant sits on the rug in the entrance hall.
explanation.definitionFit: Arugula is the American name for rocket, a salad herb.

clue.text: Irrigation device largely not working, has worked before

indicators.note: worked like dough, the letters are kneaded into a new shape
largely means most of it, so the final letter is dropped
before places one part ahead of the other

blocks.note: taken as written, ready for mixing
duff is British slang for broken or useless

explanation.surface: A watering device that mostly fails, though it has functioned before.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaduf is a pole with a bucket and counterweight, used in Egypt and the Middle East to raise water for irrigation.

clue.text: Buddy at Oxford, say with unparted hair across forehead

indicators.note: being at a place puts one part right next to the other

blocks.note: Oxford is an example of a university
bro is slang for a mate
W is the abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: A college friend at Oxford has a single brow over his eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: A unibrow is eyebrows that meet in the middle, forming one line of hair above the nose.

clue.text: Vehicle parking by edges of enormous steep slope

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its first and last letters
by means beside, so the parts sit next to each other

blocks.note: first and last letters of enormous
a car is a vehicle
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A car is parked beside a huge steep slope.
explanation.definitionFit: An escarp, or escarpment, is the steep inner bank of a ditch or any steep slope.

clue.text: Face the unknown and go around after breaking hip

indicators.note: breaking smashes the word so its letters fall into a new order
turned around, so the word faces the other way
after places one part following another

blocks.note: the letters reordered
z is a standard algebraic unknown
taken as written

explanation.surface: Facing the unknown and starting again after a hip fracture.
explanation.definitionFit: Phizog is jocular British slang for the face, from physiognomy.

clue.text: Get enthusiastic about Epiphany gift?

indicators.note: turned about, so the letters are moved around

blocks.note: to get enthusiastic is to be a fan

explanation.surface: Someone is told to show enthusiasm for an Epiphany present.
explanation.definitionFit: In Italy the Befana is the old woman who brings presents at Epiphany, and the word also means such a gift.

clue.text: Yogi's acolyte heard bird

indicators.note: heard means we go by how the name is pronounced

blocks.note: Boo-Boo is the small sidekick of Yogi Bear in the cartoons

explanation.surface: A guru's disciple listens to birdsong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yogi' suggests a meditating guru, but it is Yogi Bear, the cartoon character.
explanation.definitionFit: The boubou is an African bush-shrike whose duetting calls give it its name.

clue.text: Regularly moan how bad butter is produced from this

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: A grumble about how poorly some butter turns out.
explanation.definitionFit: The mahwa is an Indian tree whose seeds yield a fat called mahwa butter.

clue.text: Shaft of old mine finally shrouded by silence almost

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the word
almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
something shrouded is wrapped inside a cover

blocks.note: the last letter of mine
to still is to silence

explanation.surface: A disused mine shaft lies wrapped in near silence.
explanation.walkthrough: STILL loses its last L, and E goes inside: ST-E-IL. 'Of old' marks an archaic word.
explanation.definitionFit: Steil is an old spelling of steal or stale, meaning the handle or long shaft of a tool.

clue.text: Poetry reciter effectively clear

blocks.note: as in a blow that strikes home, landing with full effect
to rid a place is to clear it

explanation.surface: A performer of verse whose delivery is crisp and effective.
explanation.definitionFit: The Homeridae were rhapsodes who recited Homer's epics, so a Homerid is a performer of his poems.

clue.text: A flap with which you'd fly around?

definitions.text: A flap with which you'd fly around?

indicators.note: around means encircling, so one element goes round the other

blocks.note: the pium is a small biting Brazilian fly
a tag is a flap or loose piece hanging off something

explanation.surface: Asking what flap of skin lets a creature glide through the air.
explanation.walkthrough: A TAG goes inside PIUM: PI-A TAG-IUM. Read whole, the clue describes the membrane itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The patagium is the fold of skin between the limbs of bats and flying squirrels that lets them glide or fly.

clue.text: Firework device left out for one

indicators.note: one letter goes out and another comes in to replace it

blocks.note: a ploy is a scheme or stratagem
L is the abbreviation for left
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A firework gadget has been left out for someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Pioy is a Scots word for a homemade firework, a little cone of damp gunpowder.

clue.text: Slough, butt of Betjeman's parting reproach in poem

indicators.note: the butt of something is its end, here the final letter of the name
parting means leaving, so the letter departs from the word

blocks.note: the final letter of Betjeman
shend is an archaic poetic word meaning to reproach or disgrace

explanation.surface: Slough, the town John Betjeman famously asked friendly bombs to fall on, gets one last rebuke in verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slough' looks like the Berkshire town of Betjeman's poem, but it is the verb meaning to cast off skin. SHEND loses its N.
explanation.definitionFit: To slough is to cast off dead skin, as a snake does, which is the same as to shed it.

clue.text: Watered nothing in marshland

indicators.note: in places one element inside another

blocks.note: mire is boggy ground
O looks like a zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing has been irrigated in the swamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watered' looks like irrigated, but it describes fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Moiré is fabric with a rippled, wavy sheen, traditionally called watered silk.

clue.text: Get cottage perhaps for temporary accommodation

blocks.note: to twig is British slang for to understand
cottage is British slang for a public lavatory

explanation.surface: Someone looks for a holiday cottage as a short-term place to stay.
explanation.definitionFit: A twigloo is a makeshift shelter built of branches in trees, used by road protesters as temporary housing.

clue.text: Bing used to finish off genealogic list from Scotland

indicators.note: the finish of a word is its last letter alone

blocks.note: the last letter of genealogic
roon is Scots for a list, the selvage edge of cloth

explanation.surface: Bing finished off his family tree from Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'List' looks like a register, but it means the edge strip of woven fabric. Bing is the singer Bing Crosby.
explanation.definitionFit: Bing Crosby was the archetypal crooner, so croon is what he used to do.

clue.text: Special Italian essence and Scottish toffee mixture

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for special
alma is Italian for soul, the essence of a person
gundy is a Scots word for toffee

explanation.surface: A special mix of Italian flavouring and Scottish toffee.
explanation.definitionFit: A salmagundi is a mixed dish of chopped meats and eggs, and by extension any miscellaneous assortment.
